title: Scheduling jobs on one machine
html:
This task is about finding an optimal schedule for nnn jobs on a single machine, if the job iii can be processed in tit_iti​ time, but for the ttt seconds waiting before processing the job a penalty of fi(t)f_i(t)fi​(t) has to be paid.

Thus the task asks to find such an permutation of the jobs, so that the total penalty is minimal. If we denote by π\piπ the permutation of the jobs (π1\pi_1π1​ is the first processed item, π2\pi_2π2​ the second, etc.), then the total penalty is equal to:

F(π)=fπ1(0)+fπ2(tπ1)+fπ3(tπ1+tπ2)+⋯+fπn(∑i=1n−1tπi)F(\pi) = f_{\pi_1}(0) + f_{\pi_2}(t_{\pi_1}) + f_{\pi_3}(t_{\pi_1} + t_{\pi_2}) + \dots + f_{\pi_n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} t_{\pi_i}\right)F(π)=fπ1​​(0)+fπ2​​(tπ1​​)+fπ3​​(tπ1​​+tπ2​​)+⋯+fπn​​(i=1∑n−1​tπi​​)

Solutions for special cases

Linear penalty functions

First we will solve the problem in the case that all penalty functions fi(t)f_i(t)fi​(t) are linear, i.e. they have the form fi(t)=ci⋅tf_i(t) = c_i \cdot tfi​(t)=ci​⋅t, where cic_ici​ is a non-negative number. Note that these functions don't have a constant term. Otherwise we can sum up all constant term, and resolve the problem without them.

Let us fixate some permutation π\piπ, and take an index i=1…n−1i = 1 \dots n-1i=1…n−1. Let the permutation π′\pi'π′ be equal to the permutation π\piπ with the elements iii and i+1i+1i+1 switched. Let's see how much the penalty changed.

F(π′)−F(π)=F(\pi') - F(\pi) =F(π′)−F(π)=

It is easy to see that the changes only occur in the iii-th and (i+1)(i+1)(i+1)-th summands:

=cπi′⋅∑k=1i−1tπk′+cπi+1′⋅∑k=1itπk′−cπi⋅∑k=1i−1tπk−cπi+1⋅∑k=1itπk=cπi+1⋅∑k=1i−1tπk′+cπi⋅∑k=1itπk′−cπi⋅∑k=1i−1tπk−cπi+1⋅∑k=1itπk=cπi⋅tπi+1−cπi+1⋅tπi\begin{align} &= c_{\pi_i'} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^{i-1} t_{\pi_k'} + c_{\pi_{i+1}'} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^i t_{\pi_k'} - c_{\pi_i} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^{i-1} t_{\pi_k} - c_{\pi_{i+1}} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^i t_{\pi_k} \\ &= c_{\pi_{i+1}} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^{i-1} t_{\pi_k'} + c_{\pi_i} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^i t_{\pi_k'} - c_{\pi_i} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^{i-1} t_{\pi_k} - c_{\pi_{i+1}} \cdot \sum_{k = 1}^i t_{\pi_k} \\ &= c_{\pi_i} \cdot t_{\pi_{i+1}} - c_{\pi_{i+1}} \cdot t_{\pi_i} \end{align}​=cπi′​​⋅k=1∑i−1​tπk′​​+cπi+1′​​⋅k=1∑i​tπk′​​−cπi​​⋅k=1∑i−1​tπk​​−cπi+1​​⋅k=1∑i​tπk​​=cπi+1​​⋅k=1∑i−1​tπk′​​+cπi​​⋅k=1∑i​tπk′​​−cπi​​⋅k=1∑i−1​tπk​​−cπi+1​​⋅k=1∑i​tπk​​=cπi​​⋅tπi+1​​−cπi+1​​⋅tπi​​​​

It is easy to see, that if the schedule π\piπ is optimal, than any change in it leads to an increased penalty (or to the identical penalty), therefore for the optimal schedule we can write down the following condition:

cπi⋅tπi+1−cπi+1⋅tπi≥0∀i=1…n−1c_{\pi_{i}} \cdot t_{\pi_{i+1}} - c_{\pi_{i+1}} \cdot t_{\pi_i} \ge 0 \quad \forall i = 1 \dots n-1cπi​​⋅tπi+1​​−cπi+1​​⋅tπi​​≥0∀i=1…n−1

And after rearranging we get:

cπitπi≥cπi+1tπi+1∀i=1…n−1\frac{c_{\pi_i}}{t_{\pi_i}} \ge \frac{c_{\pi_{i+1}}}{t_{\pi_{i+1}}} \quad \forall i = 1 \dots n-1tπi​​cπi​​​≥tπi+1​​cπi+1​​​∀i=1…n−1

Thus we obtain the optimal schedule by simply sorting the jobs by the fraction citi\frac{c_i}{t_i}ti​ci​​ in non-ascending order.

It should be noted, that we constructed this algorithm by the so-called permutation method: we tried to swap two adjacent elements, calculated how much the penalty changed, and then derived the algorithm for finding the optimal method.

Exponential penalty function

Let the penalty function look like this:

fi(t)=ci⋅eα⋅t,f_i(t) = c_i \cdot e^{\alpha \cdot t},fi​(t)=ci​⋅eα⋅t,

where all numbers cic_ici​ are non-negative and the constant α\alphaα is positive.

By applying the permutation method, it is easy to determine that the jobs must be sorted in non-ascending order of the value:

vi=1−eα⋅ticiv_i = \frac{1 - e^{\alpha \cdot t_i}}{c_i}vi​=ci​1−eα⋅ti​​

Identical monotone penalty function

In this case we consider the case that all fi(t)f_i(t)fi​(t) are equal, and this function is monotone increasing.

It is obvious that in this case the optimal permutation is to arrange the jobs by non-descending processing time tit_iti​.

The Livshits-Kladov theorem

The Livshits-Kladov theorem establishes that the permutation method is only applicable for the above mentioned three cases, i.e.:

  • Linear case: fi(t)=ci(t)+dif_i(t) = c_i(t) + d_ifi​(t)=ci​(t)+di​, where cic_ici​ are non-negative constants,
  • Exponential case: fi(t)=ci⋅eα⋅t+dif_i(t) = c_i \cdot e_{\alpha \cdot t} + d_ifi​(t)=ci​⋅eα⋅t​+di​, where cic_ici​ and α\alphaα are positive constants,
  • Identical case: fi(t)=ϕ(t)f_i(t) = \phi(t)fi​(t)=ϕ(t), where ϕ\phiϕ is a monotone increasing function.

In all other cases the method cannot be applied.

The theorem is proven under the assumption that the penalty functions are sufficiently smooth (the third derivatives exists).

In all three case we apply the permutation method, through which the desired optimal schedule can be found by sorting, hence in O(nlog⁡n)O(n \log n)O(nlogn) time.
